data.name: DarkMaus
data.detailed_description:
In DarkMaus, you play a lonely wanderer searching for what's left in a corrupted world. The odds are against you - you will certainly perish.

Note: This game is designed for an Xbox Controller, but mouse / keyboard works too.

  • A worthy challenge - combat in DarkMaus is thoughtful and skill based. Enemies force you to be reactive to survive, and punish any greedy moves or mistakes. You'll start out swearing that it's impossible, and end up a god among Mäuse.
  • Death Echo - each time you die, an ally ghost is summoned that retraces your steps, fighting by your side. With time you can collect multiple ally ghosts and choose their weapons for extra strategy opportunities.
  • A dark world to explore - search for answers and secrets in the desolate land of Hazath, whose inhabitants have gone feral.
  • Combat style variety - from spears to greatswords and bows to fireballs, DarkMaus has a large number of viable builds and playstyles, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.

reviews.review:
So I beat this game twice to get both endings and all the ng+ weapons. I did so after the patches that fix some issues people talk about in other reviews (mainly no healing mid combat). I still can't recommend it.

The game is much too difficult, which is a strange negative for a souls-like. The enemies just feel unfair most of the time. They're placed in massive groups, hover just outside of reach of your weapon, and deal enough damage to end you in 2-3 blows. It doesn't help that running past them isn't much of an option as they follow you for far too long, and the time limit imposed by the torch requires you to stop at bonfires, which you can't rest at with enemies around. I should also point out in this section that while there are health potions (bread crumbs), they're a rare drop and not worth relying on. The only time you should use them is during a boss, but bosses are the easiest part of the game.

The controls are good, but turning takes time. This was an intended design decision, and while exploring it's not something you really notice. The only reason the developer even included this was to make certain enemies way harder. The different tabs you had to navigate were annoying, but when you use the provided hotkeys (1-4), it's not bad.

There was no story. I mean there was, but it never really develops, which is kind of a given for the length of this game (look at my playtime for two full playthroughs). Only a couple of npcs exist to talk to you, with only 3 contributing to the actual game.

[spoiler]
Both endings are exactly the same, and say nothing other than 'You Win'
Don't bother wasting you time on the bad ending, since it is the exact same as the rest of the game minus the final boss. It only involves an annoying amount of backtracking.
When getting the good ending, you can grab an item from Anna by not healing Destrian (which you would only know to do on a second playthrough) that prevents the hunters from spawning, but you could also prevent that by killing the final boss literally two rooms away. Why does this exist?
[/spoiler]

All in all, it's a cheap game. A little short for $5, and an aggravating level of difficulty, but it's neat conceptually and artistically. So a weak negative review from me.
